title: Which of these are metrics?

prereqs.why: Each option has to be checked against all four conditions.
Two of these are standard metrics that are worth recognising on sight.

statement:
Each line below proposes a function $d$ on a set. Select every one that **is** a metric.

Checking one means checking all four axioms; refuting one means producing a single counterexample.
hints: The four axioms again: non-negative, zero exactly on the diagonal, symmetric, and the triangle inequality.
For the ones you suspect, do not try to prove them — try to break them, with the smallest numbers you can. A counterexample is one line; a proof is four.
For option 3, ask what $d(x,y) = 0$ means when $d(x,y) = |x^2 - y^2|$ and $x$ is allowed to be negative.

payload.prompt: Select every function that is a metric.
options: On any set $X$: $d(x,y) = 0$ if $x = y$, and $1$ otherwise.
On $\R$: $d(x,y) = |x - y|$ if $x \le y$, and $2|x - y|$ if $x > y$.
